title: Smooth product charts preserve contraction and synchronize tower indices
statement:
Use fine monoschemes, fans, coherent monoid ideals, saturated blowup towers, recursive pullback, and contraction as in [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization] and [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. Let $\mathscr C$ be the full category of fine monoschemes with finite affine covers such that both their ordinary stalk group completions and the group completions of their sharpened stalks are torsion free. A smooth monoscheme morphism between objects of $\mathscr C$ sharpens to a smooth fan morphism, and $M\in\mathscr C$ is smooth if and only if $M^\sharp$ is smooth. On stalks, $P\to P\oplus\mathbf N^r\oplus\mathbf Z^t$ sharpens to $\overline P\to\overline P\oplus\mathbf N^r$. For a saturated blowup tower on $M$ and the tower on $M^\sharp$ obtained by sharpening its levels and centers, a stage has whole ideal and is an isomorphism exactly when its counterpart does; consequently their contractions retain the same ordered indices, including a nonidentity initial saturation with whole ideal.

Let $f:Y\to X$ be a smooth surjective morphism in $\mathscr C$ and let $T$ be a finite saturated blowup tower on $X$. At every recursively pulled-back level, its center is the whole sheaf exactly when the center of $T$ at that index is, and such a whole-ideal stage is an isomorphism after pullback exactly when it was before pullback. In local smooth product charts the whole recursive tower has level monoids $P_i\oplus\mathbf N^r\oplus\mathbf Z^s$, where the $P_i$ are the corresponding levels over $X$; in particular $P_i\oplus\mathbf N^r\oplus\mathbf Z^s$ is saturated exactly when $P_i$ is. The same conclusions about surjective pullback and contracted indices hold for smooth surjections of fine torsion-free fans with finite affine covers.

Let $R$ assign to every object of $\mathscr C$ a finite saturated desingularization tower and canonical identifications $R(Y)\simeq(f^*R(X))^c$ for every smooth $f:Y\to X$, preserving the centers and order and compatible with identities and composition. Then every $R(X)$ is contracted and a smooth surjection gives $R(Y)\simeq f^*R(X)$ before contraction, with every index retained. For any two smooth maps $f,g:Y\to X$, the full uncontracted towers $f^*R(X)$ and $g^*R(X)$ are canonically identified over $Y$, including all ideals and original indices. This identification is the restriction from the two smooth surjections $f\amalg1_X,g\amalg1_X:Y\amalg X\to X$.

source.place: ILO VIII 3.1.13--3.1.16, 3.1.21--3.1.26, pp.100--102, and Remark 2.3.5(i),(iii), p.92; smooth product, contraction and synchronization (returned proof steps 4--6). No Stacks tag states this monoidal-geometric result.

proof.text: At a smooth stalk map the units of $P\oplus\mathbf N^r\oplus\mathbf Z^t$ are $P^\times\oplus0\oplus\mathbf Z^t$, so taking the quotient gives exactly $\overline P\to\overline P\oplus\mathbf N^r$. This proves smoothness of the sharpened morphism by the definitions. For object smoothness, apply [lem-trf-fine-monoid-unit-splitting] separately to each stalk: both torsion-freeness hypotheses hold because $M\in\mathscr C$. Thus $P\simeq\overline P\oplus\mathbf Z^s$. If the sharp stalk is $\mathbf N^d$, this is the required smooth ordinary stalk, and the converse is the displayed quotient calculation.

source.place: VIII 3.1.13--3.1.16, p.100; unit splitting with the explicit hypotheses of the item.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-sharpening-blowup-chart-comparison], corresponding tower levels and actual ideals sharpen compatibly and remain in $\mathscr C$. Whole ideals therefore correspond at each original index. The saturated blowup of a whole ideal is just saturation: its chart at the generator $0$ is $P^{\rm sat}$. This map is an isomorphism exactly when the level is saturated. Indeed, on a stalk chart its closed point has stalk map $P\hookrightarrow P^{\rm sat}$; an element $p\in P$ becoming a unit in $P^{\rm sat}$ was already a unit, since $-np\in P$ implies $-p=-np+(n-1)p\in P$. Hence the closed point maps to the closed point and an isomorphism forces $P=P^{\rm sat}$. Conversely that equality makes each chart map the identity. At each level use [lem-trf-fine-monoid-unit-splitting] to write $P=B\oplus\mathbf Z^s$. The coordinate definition of saturation gives $P^{\rm sat}=B^{\rm sat}\oplus\mathbf Z^s$, so ordinary and sharp levels are saturated simultaneously. Here $B^{\rm sat}$ remains sharp: if $g,-g\in B^{\rm sat}$, a common positive multiple lies in $B^\times=0$, so torsion-freeness of $B^{\rm gp}$ gives $g=0$. Thus precisely the same indices are deleted, and a whole-ideal nonidentity initial saturation is retained on both sides.

source.place: VIII 3.1.17--3.1.25, pp.101--102; contraction convention as in the two definition nodes.

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-fine-monoid-local-smooth-charts] to cover $f$ by $P\to P\oplus K$, $K=\mathbf N^r\oplus\mathbf Z^s$. For a center $I\subset P$ its extension is $I\oplus K$. At a generator $(a,0)$ the fraction chart is $P[I-a]\oplus K$: each new fraction is $(b-a,0)$ and the original monoid already supplies every $K$-coordinate. In $(P[I-a])^{\rm gp}\oplus\mathbf Z^r\oplus\mathbf Z^s$, the saturation condition is coordinatewise, giving $(P[I-a])^{\rm sat}\oplus K$, because $nv\in\mathbf N^r$ for $n>0$ forces $v\in\mathbf N^r$. The overlaps localize at $(b-a,0)$, so these identities agree on overlaps. Induct on the index, starting with the displayed chart at level zero. The recursive blowup definition and this calculation supply the same product description at the next level, with the extended next center. This proves the claimed description of the whole tower, with fixed $K$ on each initial product chart. It also proves that each level map is smooth and that a product level is saturated exactly when its $P_i$ factor is.

source.place: VIII 3.1.19--3.1.23, p.101; product-chart calculation expanding Remark 3.1.23.

proof.text: Surjectivity persists at every level, as follows directly from the charts in Step 3. Given $x_i$ in a target level, choose $y_0$ over its image $x_0$ and a product chart at $y_0$. The entire target tower over this neighborhood is covered by the fraction charts $P_i$ of Step 3. For any prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset P_i$, the subset $\mathfrak p\times K$ is prime in $P_i\oplus K$: its complement is $(P_i\setminus\mathfrak p)\times K$ and is a submonoid. It contracts to $\mathfrak p$, yielding a point over $x_i$. At any such lifted point, locality of the stalk map shows that an extended ideal is whole exactly when the target stalk ideal is whole: a sum $\phi(a)+q=0$ with $a$ in the ideal forces $\phi(a)$ to be a unit, hence $a$ to be a unit, hence the ideal to contain $0$. Whole ideals certainly pull back to whole ideals. Since every target point lifts, this tests the whole sheaf in both directions at each original index.

source.place: VIII 3.1.5, 3.1.16, 3.1.22--3.1.23, pp.99--101; explicit prime-ideal and local-unit calculation.

proof.text: For a whole center, Step 2 identifies its saturated blowup with saturation. On every product chart Step 3 gives $P_i^{\rm sat}\oplus K$ and shows that $P_i\oplus K$ is saturated exactly when $P_i$ is. The charts over lifted points from Step 4 cover the target levels, so saturation, and hence the isomorphism condition for a whole-center stage, is reflected as well as preserved. Combining this with Step 4 proves equality of the ordered retained index sets, including the first saturation if it is nonidentity. Proper principal centers are never deleted merely because their blowup is an isomorphism: the definition also requires the whole ideal.

For fans apply the fan product-chart assertion of [lem-trf-fine-monoid-local-smooth-charts]. Repeat the fraction calculations of Step 3 with $s=0$ and sharpen each fraction chart as required in [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. The units of $A\oplus\mathbf N^r$ are $A^\times\oplus0$, so its sharpening is $\overline A\oplus\mathbf N^r$; all chart maps and overlap fractions are unchanged in the first coordinate. The prime $\mathfrak p\times\mathbf N^r$ and the local-unit test of Step 4 give surjectivity and whole-center reflection at every level. Finally the whole-center chart at an original sharp stalk $P$ is $P^{\rm sat}$ with its sharp sheaf; it is unchanged exactly when $P$ is saturated. To see that $P^{\rm sat}$ is sharp here, if both $g$ and $-g$ lie in it, a common positive multiple lies in $P^\times=0$, and torsion-freeness of $P^{\rm gp}$ gives $g=0$. Thus the coordinate saturation test also reflects isomorphisms for whole-center stages, proving exactly the fan assertions.

source.place: VIII 3.1.16(ii), 3.1.17, 3.1.24, pp.100--102; fan product and sharpening calculations.

proof.text: Apply the stipulated comparison of $R$ to $1_X$. Its full pullback is $R(X)$ itself by the recursive definition, so $R(X)\simeq R(X)^c$ as finite ordered towers. If its length is $n$ and $d$ stages are deleted, this isomorphism forces $n=n-d$ and hence $d=0$. Every assigned tower is therefore contracted. For a smooth surjection $f$, Steps 4--5 show that no index of $f^*R(X)$ is deletable because none of $R(X)$ is. The stipulated contracted comparison is consequently already the center-preserving full comparison $R(Y)\simeq f^*R(X)$, with all original indices.

source.place: VIII 3.1.26, p.102 and Remark 2.3.5(i), p.92; identity and surjective comparisons.

proof.text: Set $U=Y\amalg X$, $F=f\amalg1_X$ and $G=g\amalg1_X$. The finite affine covers combine and the stalk groups are those of the components, so $U\in\mathscr C$. On its two open components $F$ (respectively $G$) is $f$ (respectively $g$) or the identity; hence both maps are smooth, and both are surjective because of the $X$ component. Step 7 identifies both $F^*R(X)$ and $G^*R(X)$ with the single tower $R(U)$. Compose these specified comparisons and restrict every level and every ideal to the open component $Y$. The recursive chart definition says that these restrictions are exactly $f^*R(X)$ and $g^*R(X)$, before any contraction. Thus their comparison preserves the common original index at every stage, even when a restricted whole-ideal stage is an identity. Its canonicity and compatibility are those of the stipulated comparisons of $R$ and their restriction; this is precisely the identification asserted in the item.

proof_origin.place: VIII 3.1.13--3.1.26 and Remark 2.3.5(i),(iii), pp.92,100--102; explicit saturated product-chart expansion of the source argument.
